verdict.rationale: Paperspace documents creating GPU machines from the console, API, or CLI, offers an "ML in a Box" template with frameworks and CUDA preinstalled, and supports SSH with root access, so the core provisioning path exists. The "within minutes" claim rests only on marketing copy. High-end GPUs such as the H100 need approval first, and one hands-on user reported that getting SSH access was an uphill battle, which undercuts the fast time-to-running-code part of the story. missing for 10: independent evidence of provisioning-to-running-code time, on-demand GPU access without approval gates for high-end types, and corroborated smooth SSH onboarding.

support.subject: As a developer, I can provision an on-demand GPU instance from the console or API and be running code on it within minutes

citations.quote: You can create a Linux machine using the Paperspace console, Paperspace API, or Paperspace CLI.
Machines are Linux and Windows virtual machines with persistent storage, GPU options, and free unlimited bandwidth.
Choose "ML in a Box" template that comes preinstalled with all the major ML frameworks and CUDA® drivers.
Bring your SSH key and connect directly to your VM with full root access.
Go from signup to training a model in seconds
If you choose any high-end machines, such as NVIDIA H100, you need to request for approval to use them.
